title: I started without a coding background. My AI-assisted soulslike is now in Season 2
author: DoubleJayM
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/7rzj8ogpn2sh1.png?width=850&format=png&auto=webp&s=978acc835ada4ba7dcf49b65a564713625deaf92



Hi everyone. I'm the developer of Broken Soul: Season 2, a mobile soulslike built around real-time boss fights on a 5x2 grid. I started without a programming background because I wanted to make the kind of game I enjoy. The game has been running for over a year, and I've recently made a substantial update to the Android version.

https://preview.redd.it/4ivce9dqn2sh1.png?width=850&format=png&auto=webp&s=361e94b2d2c85257cd639b68750b331cec3fa2d1

  


The combat is about reading an attack, choosing where to move, and deciding whether you can squeeze in one more hit. You control attacks, dodges and guards yourself, with stamina and action timing limiting what you can safely do. The grid makes positioning part of the fight: both when you react and where you move matter.

https://preview.redd.it/8ze18q1rn2sh1.png?width=850&format=png&auto=webp&s=9702bfaf5e0815ad7d7413d4ce89c3ac534389d7

  


For the AI development side, I've been using Codex for code implementation and debugging, alongside AI-generated artwork. Recent work has included animating 2D characters, touch controls and the early tutorial flow. I break changes into specific tasks, check how they interact with the existing game, and iterate on the result.

One concrete example is adding a character action. Getting the animation is only part of it: the sprite position and size, hit timing, touch input, and transition back to idle all need to agree. Those details are where much of the iteration goes. The same applies to a tutorial: having a guard mechanic working doesn't automatically make it clear to someone playing for the first time.

I'm sharing my own commercial game here. It's free to download on Android, with in-app purchases and ads. The attached images are actual game screenshots from the Korean version; English is also supported.

https://preview.redd.it/rm5o56urn2sh1.png?width=1280&format=png&auto=webp&s=5903fe4cf8f901bcec149cfeafdda39bf8c387cf

  


Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=xyz.brokensoul.mygame](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=xyz.brokensoul.mygame)

For other developers working on AI-assisted action games, how do you check whether an attack is readable and the controls feel responsive? And if you try this one, I'd appreciate knowing where the first fight feels confusing or awkward. That's a part of the game I'm continuing to work on.
